Bishop's Hill fully demolished, residents did not protest

Su said he received a demolition notice at the end of July and immediately contacted Sham Shui Po District Council members to request the retention of the fitness facilities on Wozi Hill, but was told that "no facilities would be preserved." Su pointed out that residents had previously launched petitions to protest the demolition, but this time the notice period was too short to organise opposition. As a result, a morning exercise spot used by residents for over 20 years will disappear.

Three days ago (the 10th), the Home Affairs Department announced the Wozi Hill enhancement plan, stating that the government would clear unauthorised and unsafe structures, facilities, or杂物 on the hill in phases, pointing out that these items had long been illegally occupying government land.

Yesterday morning (the 12th), around 6:30 a.m., personnel from the Lands Department and uniformed police officers arrived and cordoned off the slope rest area on Tong Ying Street from the foot of the hill to the summit. Movers immediately began removing fitness equipment, bicycles, ping-pong tables, and other items. Police deployed冲锋车 (unmarked vehicles) and 豬籠車 (prison vans) for security. Su said this was merely a place where residents exercised, and he did not understand the purpose of the police deployment. "The officers just stood there, monitoring us the whole time. What did we do wrong? Are we rioters? Have we broken the law?"

"Morning exercise hotspot" becomes LCSD facilities

Su pointed out that residents crowdfunded HK$400,000 to build the Bishop's Hill "morning exercise hotspot," including ping-pong tables, fitness equipment, and unofficial hiking trails built by themselves decades ago. On the day of demolition, many residents were still doing morning exercises and using the fitness equipment. Several residents were deeply saddened by the loss of this sports ground they had used for many years. Some residents kept asking Mr. Su what to do, but Mr. Su himself did not know what to say.

He said he had spent several days moving the fitness equipment away, hoping to preserve what he had built with his own hands. Currently, he has moved all the muscle massage rollers, and some residents plan to move parts of the deity statues to Lantau Island.

According to the Home Affairs Department's Wozi Hill enhancement plan, the "morning exercise hotspot" will be converted into LCSD facilities. The homemade fitness equipment on the hill will be replaced by standard LCSD recreational and sports facilities; as for the deity statues, religious personnel will come to handle them properly.

Miraculous recovery gave rise to Bishop's Hill "morning exercise hotspot"

75-year-old Su Chi-keung is a SARS survivor. Due to side effects of medication, he suffered from后遗症 including muscle pain, weakness, and fatigue. After three years of physiotherapy, his condition did not improve. In 2008, at a neighbour's invitation, Su went to Bishop's Hill. After doing morning exercises, he felt his spirits lift, which he attributed to the fresh air on the hill. He then began exercising on Bishop's Hill every morning at 6 a.m. After persisting for one month, he recovered his health and stamina and decided to stop physiotherapy.

In 2009, Mr. Su travelled to Korea and was inspired by the local fitness facilities. After returning to Hong Kong, he referenced the designs and "DIY" a stationary bike and a resistance machine at his own hardware factory. He single-handedly carried the fitness equipment up Bishop's Hill piece by piece, saying the manufacturing process was simple but the搬运 was extremely arduous. Over four years, he built more than 20 fitness facilities on Bishop's Hill, including swings, balance beams, and rollers, installed on the vacant land above the current Sham Shui Po service reservoir. At the time, some elderly people objected, but after other residents used them and found that their physical discomfort was alleviated, the facilities became very popular.

Bishop's Hill's first exposure, residents protest demolition

Su pointed out that in 2014, more than 200 young people held a wild party on Bishop's Hill, creating a noise nuisance. After police arrived, they discovered for the first time a large number of private fitness facilities. Subsequently, the Water Supplies Department stepped up patrols of Bishop's Hill, repeatedly驱赶 residents exercising on the hill, and planned to demolish the facilities. At that time, Mr. Su launched several protests and personally went to the Sham Shui Po District Council Secretariat to争取 the retention of the fitness area.

Accidental viral fame makes Bishop's Hill service reservoir a Grade I historic building

In 2017, the Water Supplies Department planned to demolish unauthorised structures on Bishop's Hill and return the land to the Lands Department. Additionally, the roots of two large trees on top of the service reservoir had extended into the structures, posing a collapse risk, and government departments prepared to remove the trees and backfill the reservoir. In 2020, the Water Supplies Department promised Mr. Su that his fitness facilities could be placed on the land after backfilling, and Su agreed to the works.

However, on Christmas Eve, Mr. Su and a volunteer sneaked into the service reservoir to check whether any items had been left behind, and posted photos on social media, attracting large numbers of citizens to visit the reservoir and drawing public attention. Su pointed out that the public protested the demolition due to the historical value of the service reservoir. A Ms. Fang, who frequently visited Bishop's Hill, even stood in front of an excavator to stop the demolition work.

In 2021, the service reservoir was assessed by the Antiquities Advisory Board as a Grade I historic building. The service reservoir was preserved and opened to the public, and Mr. Su relocated the fitness facilities to the foot of the hill.

The Mao Zedong statue incident may have triggered the demolition

In June 2022, the Sham Shui Po District Management Committee planned to remove the altar and fitness facilities. Mr. Su launched a petition to request the retention of these facilities, stating that he obtained signatures from 3,399 Sham Shui Po District residents and submitted a letter to the Home Affairs Department, pledging not to expand the facilities further.

Su pointed out that Bishop's Hill had remained peaceful thereafter, and the government had not indicated any need for demolition. However, in early 2026, resident Ms. Fang set up a Mao Zedong statue and Mao Zedong cultural hall on Bishop's Hill. Although they were later removed, Su believes the Mao Zedong incident caused the government to refocus on Bishop's Hill. Coupled with some residents making loud noises on the hill and disturbing nearby residents, the government decided to fully demolish Bishop's Hill.

In early 2026, resident Ms. Fang set up a Mao Zedong statue and Mao Zedong cultural hall on Bishop's Hill, once again sparking controversy over the hill's use. (File photo)

"Without Bishop's Hill, I would have lived 20 years less"

Watching workers dismantle the fitness equipment he had personally built one by one, Su did not show sadness. He plans to move the dismantled fitness equipment back to his home and continue telling the media about the history of Bishop's Hill. In fact, he knows full well that Bishop's Hill is highly controversial and the "morning exercise hotspot" had been unauthorised for many years, but he believes this place has benefited many residents over the long term. He hopes that by telling the story of Bishop's Hill, he will gain the government's recognition. Although the venue ultimately could not be preserved, he still hopes to pass the story on, in gratitude for everything Bishop's Hill has given him.

He bid farewell to Bishop's Hill: "Thank it for giving me a new life. Without it, I would have died 20 years sooner. I was supposed to be dead. If not for Bishop's Hill, I would already be dead... Besides, I'm a SARS-injured survivor. Do you think I could still be alive today?"
